clue.text: Surreptitious way to get Cockney well

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops the aitch at the start of a word

parts.note: well in the sense of in good health

explanation.surface: A Londoner asking the furtive route to recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' signals the dropped H, turning HEALTHY into EALTHY. Cockney is the working-class London accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy movement is quiet and secret, just as surreptitious action is.

clue.text: Like this, paper is easy to cut

definitions.text: Like this, paper is easy to cut

parts.words: Like this, paper is easy to cut
parts.note: read as a quality of paper that makes it yield easily to scissors

explanation.surface: Paper of a certain kind cuts easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Something yielding and not hard gives way readily to a blade.

clue.text: Noble organ loft frequently abandoned

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

indicators.note: the word for frequently is left out of loft

parts.note: oft is a poetic word meaning often

explanation.surface: A church organ loft that is often deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OFT from LOFT leaves just L.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: Sole, tuna, and tail of whiting cooked as seafood

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are reworked
the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fish recipe combining sole, tuna and a scrap of whiting.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish names are fodder, not definitions: SOLE, TUNA and G (tail of whiting) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A langouste is the spiny lobster or crawfish, eaten as shellfish.

clue.text: Repeat prescription that covers pet

explanation.surface: A doctor renewing medicine for the household pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the old remedy of another drink to cure a hangover; the second is literal fur on a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A further alcoholic drink taken to ease a hangover; literally, the fur growing on a dog.

clue.text: Colonialist that used to have colossal statue

definitions.text: that used to have colossal statue

explanation.surface: An empire-builder once commemorated by a giant monument.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Rhodes was the British imperialist in southern Africa; the Greek island of Rhodes had the Colossus, one of the Seven Wonders.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are proper names: the imperialist Cecil, and the island famed for its ancient bronze Colossus.

clue.text: Sun god's burden — must banish cold

indicators.note: the word for burden has to get rid of the letter for cold

parts.note: a burden is the refrain of a song
C stands for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A deity's heavy load that has to shed the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' means a song's refrain here, not a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus was the falcon-headed Egyptian deity of the sky and sun.

clue.text: Child denied treat might produce desired answer

explanation.surface: A refused child's mischief achieving what was wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: At Halloween, children say 'trick or treat': if denied the treat they play a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To be effective or achieve the result wanted; also playing a prank when refused sweets.

clue.text: Celebrated girls given light protection

parts.note: sung as in praised in song
lasses are girls, chiefly in northern English and Scottish usage

explanation.surface: Famous young women offered some flimsy safeguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinted glasses shield the eyes from bright light.

clue.text: Warning: name to be used as spelled for legal purposes

parts.note: the golfer's shout of warning to those ahead
sic, Latin for thus, marks a word to be read exactly as written

explanation.surface: A caution that a name must be kept exactly as written in a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic evidence or argument is that used in courts of law.

clue.text: Secret animal in this labyrinth? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Secret animal in this labyrinth? Just the opposite

indicators.text: in this labyrinth? Just the opposite
indicators.note: instead of the beast being inside the maze, the maze's adjective sits inside the words Secret animal

explanation.surface: A riddle about a hidden beast lurking in a famous maze.
explanation.walkthrough: The Minotaur was kept in the labyrinth on Crete; reversing the idea, the Cretan word lies within 'seCRET ANimal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary labyrinth of King Minos stood on Crete, so it is a Cretan one.

clue.text: Spectacular way to learn history, in two senses

definitions.text: Spectacular way to learn history, in two senses

parts.words: Spectacular way to learn history, in two senses
parts.note: read as a show at a historic site using sound and light, the two senses of hearing and sight

explanation.surface: A dramatic history lesson engaging two of the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A night-time entertainment at a historic building narrating its past with recorded sound and lighting.

clue.text: Unaided battle to secure plant

parts.note: doing something solo means with no help
Mons in Belgium was the site of a First World War battle
to seal is to close up securely

explanation.surface: A lone fight to save a plant from destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland plant of the lily family with arching stems and hanging white flowers.

clue.text: One spotted next to green room, daydreaming

parts.note: in snooker the brown ball is placed on its spot next to the green
a study is a room for reading or work

explanation.surface: A spotty person beside a green room, lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, coloured balls are returned to fixed spots; the brown's spot sits between green and yellow on the baulk line.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown study is a state of deep absorbed thought or reverie.

clue.text: Like dismissed monk, not working

explanation.surface: A monk thrown out who no longer functions.
explanation.walkthrough: A monk expelled is literally put outside his religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken down and not functioning; also expelled from a religious community.

clue.text: Decisively defeats opposition party on the right

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it, so the party comes after the letter

parts.note: the outs are the party currently out of office

explanation.surface: A landslide crushing the parliamentary opposition on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an enemy is to beat them overwhelmingly and put them to flight.

clue.text: Treasury star he's brought in

indicators.note: the words he's are taken inside the star sign, as a newcomer is brought into a room

parts.note: Taurus, the Bull, is a constellation and star sign
taken as its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man joining the Treasury as a rising star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasury' is the definition in its sense of a storehouse of words; it is not the government department.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a store or collection of words, from the Greek for treasure-house.

clue.text: Die in a limited rising

indicators.note: the word for die goes inside the word for limited

parts.note: scant means barely sufficient
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: Death within a restricted ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ascendant is climbing or gaining in power.

clue.text: Nothing needed at table except this bread?

definitions.text: Nothing needed at table except this bread?

parts.words: Nothing needed at table except this bread?
parts.note: read as a loaf so complete it needs nothing else to make a full meal

explanation.surface: A diner insisting this loaf alone is enough to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made from unrefined flour using the entire grain, punned on as an entire repast.

clue.text: Store has incomplete seal

indicators.note: the seal word is left short of its last letter

parts.note: a cachet is an official seal or stamp

explanation.surface: A shop with only part of a stamp in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden hoard or stock of goods.

clue.text: Imposed diet or non-civil assembly

parts.note: being short with someone means being curt or rude
the Commons is the elected house of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: Parliament forced onto rations, or else a rowdy gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Commons is the lower chamber of the British Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Short commons means scant rations, a meagre allowance of food given to someone.

clue.text: Put these people on drug? That's the idea

parts.note: them refers to a group of people
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Suggesting that some people be given drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the main subject or underlying concept of something.

clue.text: Part of ship made of very immature oak?

explanation.surface: A ship's spar crafted from a very young tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Mast is also the collective name for acorns and beech nuts, an oak at its earliest stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright spar carrying sails; also fallen acorns, from which oaks grow.

clue.text: PM once announced such a lot of changes

indicators.note: spoken out, so the statesman's name is heard and a like-sounding word written

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister declaring many reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' is bell-ringing jargon for orders in which a set of bells is rung.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a long sequence of changes rung on church bells.

clue.text: Modest cover is revived?

explanation.surface: Underwear brought back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as UN-DIES: someone who 'un-dies' is revived.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear covers the body for modesty; split, the word playfully means reverses death.

clue.text: Brought back to conscious state

indicators.note: the word for brought is turned to run back to front

parts.note: led as past tense of lead, to bring along
aware means conscious of something

explanation.surface: A patient revived to full consciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like part of 'conscious state' but is the definition: a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the United States, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: Very quick delivery arriving on foot perhaps

definitions.text: Very quick delivery arriving on foot perhaps

parts.words: Very quick delivery arriving on foot perhaps
parts.note: read as a cricket ball bowled fast that pitches right at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: An express parcel brought by a courier walking.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball; this kind is aimed at the batsman's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast ball pitched at the batter's feet so it passes under the bat.

clue.text: Taking pledge — eighteen, of course?

explanation.surface: Swearing off drink at eighteen, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf course has eighteen tees, so its tee total is eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has taken the pledge has sworn never to drink alcohol; split, the word is a count of golf tees.
